   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document\n\nThis document covers «Council Regulation (EC) No 1420/1999 of 29 April 1999 establishing common rules and procedures to apply to shipments to certain non-OECD countries of certain types of waste», published as «Official Journal L 166 , 01/07/1999». It is a Community rule on which waste may leave the Community for countries outside the OECD waste-movement decision. Its legal reach is stated in one sentence: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» The text captured here is the 1999 original; it states nothing on whether a later act changed or replaced it, so whether it still governs a lane today is a point for counsel. What the Regulation says is quoted; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:*, and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.\n\n## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace\n\nThe Regulation sorts non-OECD destination countries into two lists and gives each list its own rule. Article 1: «The export of waste listed in Annex II to Regulation (EEC) No 259/93 and mentioned in Annex A to this Regulation to countries listed in said Annex A shall be prohibited.» Article 2: «The control procedure laid down in Article 15 of Regulation (EEC) No 259/93 shall apply to exports to the countries listed in Annex B to this Regulation with respect to those categories of waste destined for recovery only and listed in Annex II to Regulation (EEC) No 259/93.»\n\nThe reasons are given in the preamble. A country that has said it does not want a type of waste is to be obeyed: «in the case of countries which have replied that they do not wish to receive some or all types of waste listed in Annex II to the said Regulation, their will must be respected and therefore those types of waste cannot be exported to those countries». A country that has said nothing is not treated as agreeing: «in the case of countries which have not replied, silence cannot be taken as implying consent».\n\n*Analytical inference:* a freight business is affected when it is asked to arrange the export of waste destined for recovery to a country outside the OECD decision. For an Annex A country the Regulation says the export is prohibited; for an Annex B country it says the Article 15 control procedure applies, and the steps of that procedure are not in the captured text. The Regulation does not say who must refrain from the export or who must follow the procedure.\n\n## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action\n\nMONITORING: no dated step in the text falls on a freight business, and the Regulation states no cost or penalty. The practical step is a check made before any quote for waste going to a non-OECD country.\n\n- An operations lead looks up the destination country in Annex A and in Annex B before quoting a waste-for-recovery export, and reads the entry's exceptions for the waste section concerned.\n- A compliance lead asks counsel in writing whether this 1999 Regulation is still the governing text for the destination country.\n\n*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on Articles 1 and 2 above, which turn on the country listed; an entry such as «BRAZIL All types except: 1. In Section GA» shows that a country entry can carry exceptions, so the country alone does not settle the answer. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a quote for such an export can proceed for the destination and waste section concerned.\n\n## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain\n\nThe Regulation names the Council, the Commission, the Member States, the country of destination and a Committee. Article 3 sets the Commission's part when a country changes its position: «The Commission shall inform the Member States of the change of position of a country of destination within 21 days of receipt of the request from that country and shall submit its proposed determination to the Committee established under said Article 18 of Directive 75/442/EEC as soon as possible within three months of receipt of the request.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* no exporter, freight forwarder or transport operator is named. The prohibition in Article 1 speaks of the export itself, so which party in a shipment is bound by it is not stated. The Member States are the party told of a change, and the text sets no duty on a private party to follow it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which party in a waste export, the waste holder, the exporter or the party arranging the movement, falls under Articles 1 and 2.\n\n## 8. Substantive Requirements\n\nProhibition for Annex A countries. «The export of waste listed in Annex II to Regulation (EEC) No 259/93 and mentioned in Annex A to this Regulation to countries listed in said Annex A shall be prohibited.»\n\nControl procedure for Annex B countries. «The control procedure laid down in Article 15 of Regulation (EEC) No 259/93 shall apply to exports to the countries listed in Annex B to this Regulation with respect to those categories of waste destined for recovery only and listed in Annex II to Regulation (EEC) No 259/93.»\n\nChanging a country's status. «Upon request by the country of destination the control procedure applicable to that country under this Regulation shall be amended in accordance with this Article.» The Commission decides which procedure applies, and may also change it after an exceptional event; Article 3 gives as examples war, natural disaster or a trade embargo decided by the United Nations. The Commission also keeps the lists current: «The Commission shall, in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 18 of Directive 75/442/EEC, regularly review Annexes A and B of this Regulation, in order to bring them into line with the amendments made to the Annexes to Regulation (EEC) No 259/93.»\n\nReview. «The control procedures established by this Regulation shall be subject to periodic review by the Commission and for the first time no later than nine months following its publication in the Official Journal»\n\nLists and scope. Annex A is headed «Countries and territories which have indicated to the Commission that they do not wish to receive shipments for recovery of certain types of waste listed in Annex II to Council Regulation (EEC) No 259/93», and Annex B is headed «Countries and territories which have not responded to the Commission's communications on shipments for recovery of certain types of waste listed in Annex II to Council Regulation (EEC) No 259/93». A country entry can be a flat «ANDORRA All types» or an «BRAZIL All types except: 1. In Section GA». The preamble also carves some items out: «it must be made clear that such items are excluded from the scope of this Regulation».\n\n*Analytical inference:* the Regulation puts a ban or a control procedure on the export, depending on the list; it adds no fee, no deadline for a private party and no sanction.\n\n*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Article 1 prohibition and the Article 2 control procedure bind a freight business that arranges, but does not itself make, the export. No penalty or enforcement body is stated in the text, so the consequence of a breach is also a point for counsel.\n\nNo phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 6.\n\nObligations surveyed: 5; workspace-adjacent: 2; extracted as FACT: 9.\n\n## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations\n\nThe text sets no registration or reporting duty on a private party. The reporting duties it does set run between public bodies: the Commission informs the Member States of a change within 21 days, and the Commission reviews the lists: «The Commission shall, in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 18 of Directive 75/442/EEC, regularly review Annexes A and B of this Regulation, in order to bring them into line with the amendments made to the Annexes to Regulation (EEC) No 259/93.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the control procedure that Article 2 sends Annex B exports to is laid down in Article 15 of Regulation (EEC) No 259/93, and its forms and steps are not in the captured text, so what a freight business would have to file for an Annex B country is a gap that counsel or the earlier Regulation would fill.\n\n## 11. Operational System Requirements\n\nMONITORING: the text requires no system to be built. The operational need that follows from its form is a lookup that matches a destination country and a waste section code to the Annex entries, because the entries are written by section, for example «BRAZIL All types except: 1. In Section GA». The Annex A and Annex B lists are the data such a lookup would hold.\n\n*Analytical inference:* the section codes (GA, GB and others) refer to the waste list in Regulation (EEC) No 259/93, which is not in the captured text, so the lookup cannot be completed from this Regulation alone. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which edition of the country lists applies, since Article 3 allows the Commission to amend them.\n\n## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases\n\nTwo kinds of carve-out appear. In the Annexes, a country entry may be limited by an exception, as in «BRAZIL All types except: 1. In Section GA». In the preamble, items excluded for a treaty reason: «it must be made clear that such items are excluded from the scope of this Regulation».\n\n*Analytical inference:* an exception in a country entry narrows the ban or the control procedure only for the waste sections it lists. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given waste description falls inside a listed exception for the destination country.\n\n## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline\n\n- 29 April 1999: Council adopts the Regulation («Done at Luxembourg, 29 April 1999.»)\n- 01/07/1999: published in the Official Journal («Official Journal L 166 , 01/07/1999»)\n- 90th day after publication: the Regulation enters into force («This Regulation shall enter into force on the 90th day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Communities.»)\n- Within nine months after publication: first periodic review by the Commission, which may make new proposals to the Council\n\n*Analytical inference:* the 90th day is counted from publication; the text states no calendar date for it and no later dated step for a private party.\n\n## 15. Sources\n\n- Council Regulation (EC) No 1420/1999, Council of the European Union, EUR-Lex: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31999R1420\n",

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document\n\nThis document covers The Single Use Carrier Bags Charge (Wales) Regulations 2010, a Welsh Statutory Instrument (2010 No. 2880 (W. 238)) with this heading: «Made 30 November 2010 Coming into force 1 October 2011». The Regulations make a shop or a seller who delivers goods to Wales charge a minimum price for a single use carrier bag. Their reach is stated in one sentence: «These Regulations apply in relation to Wales and come into force on 1 October 2011.» What the Regulations say is quoted; what that means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:*, and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.\n\n## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace\n\nThe Regulations set a charge on bags. «A seller must charge for every single use carrier bag supplied new», and «The amount that a seller must charge is such amount as ensures that the consideration paid by a customer for each single use carrier bag is not less than 5 pence.» The charge applies in two settings: «(a) at the place in Wales where the goods are sold, for the purpose of enabling the goods to be taken away; (b) for the purpose of enabling the goods to be delivered to persons in Wales.»\n\nA single use carrier bag is a bag of a stated description: «(a) it is made wholly or mainly of paper, plant-based material or natural starch; and (b) it is not specifically manufactured for multiple reuse.» A plastic bag is caught by its size and thickness: «(b) at least one of the bag's dimensions is greater than 439 mm; (c) the bag is manufactured from material which is greater than 49 microns in thickness.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the rule is a retail rule for the person who sells goods, not a rule on moving cargo. A freight business meets it where it sells goods that are delivered to people in Wales, because the definition of a seller reaches such a person; the text names no freight forwarder or carrier. The seller is defined as «means a person who in the course of trade or business» who «(a) sells goods from a place in Wales; (b) sells goods which are delivered to persons in Wales.»\n\n## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action\n\nMONITORING: the Regulations are in force and set a charge and record duties on sellers, but they name no step for a freight business and no deadline falls on one. The action is a check of the business's own trade.\n\n- A commercial lead lists the lines of business in which the company itself sells goods, as opposed to moving a customer's goods, to persons in Wales, and notes whether a carrier bag is supplied with them.\n- A compliance lead asks counsel whether the company counts as a seller under the Regulations for any such line.\n\n*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the seller definition above. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any line of the business makes it a seller for goods delivered in Wales, and whether the courier-bag exemption quoted in section 12 covers the bag in question.\n\n## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain\n\nThe Regulations name the seller, the customer, the administrator, the Welsh Ministers and members of the public. The administrator is the local council: «A local authority is to administer the provision made by these Regulations and accordingly, is the administrator for its area», where «the reference to a local authority is a reference to a county or county borough council.» An employee does not carry the duty: «Where a person (A) sells goods in A's capacity as an officer or employee of another person (B), then for the purposes of these Regulations B is the seller in those circumstances, and not A.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a freight business sits outside the chain unless it sells goods itself. A forwarder that only moves goods sold by someone else is not named, so the seller duty would fall on the person who sells. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the role of a business that sells and delivers its own goods into Wales.\n\n## 8. Substantive Requirements\n\nCharge. «A seller must charge for every single use carrier bag supplied new», and «The amount that a seller must charge is such amount as ensures that the consideration paid by a customer for each single use carrier bag is not less than 5 pence.»\n\nRecords. The records duty applies to a seller of a size set in the text: «The condition is that on the first day of the reporting year the seller employs ten or more full time equivalent members of staff». «A seller must keep a record of the information specified in paragraph (3) for every reporting year.» «Records must be retained by a seller for a period of three years beginning on 31 May in the reporting year following that to which a record relates.» On request in writing, «the seller must provide a copy of that record to the person who requested it within 28 days of receiving the written request.»\n\nPublication. A seller must publish its record if two conditions are met, one being «(b) that the seller supplies 1000 or more single use carrier bags which attract the charge.» «A seller must publish the record on or before 31 May in the reporting year following that to which the record relates.»\n\nBags outside the charge. Schedule 1 lists them: «The kinds of single use carrier bags to which regulation 6 does not apply are».\n\nBreach and enforcement. «A seller breaches these Regulations if, as a result of having failed to take all reasonable steps necessary to enable it to do so, a seller fails to comply with a requirement mentioned in paragraph (2).» «An administrator may by notice impose a fixed monetary penalty on a seller who breaches these Regulations in the circumstances specified in regulation 11(1).» The fixed penalty table reads: «Failure to comply with the requirement to charge in accordance with regulation 6 (regulation 11(1) and (2)) £200 £100». Variable penalties have maxima: «Failure to comply with the requirement to charge in accordance with regulation 6 (regulation 11(1) and (2)) £5,000», and «Without reasonable cause, giving false or misleading information to an administrator (regulation 11(3)) £20,000».\n\n*Analytical inference:* the penalty for a failure to charge is £200 with a specified sum of £100 in the fixed penalty table, and the variable penalty for the same failure has a maximum of £5,000; both fall on the seller, not on a carrier of the goods.\n\nNo phase-in is stated in Sections 6 to 10.\n\n*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is a seller for any delivery into Wales, and so subject to the charge, the records and the penalties.\n\nObligations surveyed: 5; workspace-adjacent: 1; extracted as FACT: 14.\n\n## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations\n\nThe Regulations set no registration, but they set record and publication duties on a seller: «A seller must keep a record of the information specified in paragraph (3) for every reporting year.» «A seller must publish the record on or before 31 May in the reporting year following that to which the record relates.» A seller must also give a copy of a record on written request: «the seller must provide a copy of that record to the person who requested it within 28 days of receiving the written request.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* these duties apply only to a seller of the size stated in the text, and the publication duty only to a seller that meets both conditions, including «(b) that the seller supplies 1000 or more single use carrier bags which attract the charge.»\n\n## 11. Operational System Requirements\n\nMONITORING: the text requires a seller to count bags and money. For each reporting year the record covers the number of bags charged for and the amount received, so a seller needs a count by reporting year. This falls on a seller alone: «A seller must keep a record of the information specified in paragraph (3) for every reporting year.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a business that is not a seller needs no such system under these Regulations. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business has any seller line that needs the count.\n\n## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases\n\nSchedule 1 lists bags outside the charge: «The kinds of single use carrier bags to which regulation 6 does not apply are». Among them are «(i) mail order dispatch and courier bags;», «(g) bags used to contain purchases made on board ships, trains, aircraft, coaches or buses;» and «(m) gusseted liners used to line or cover boxes, crates or other containers of a similar nature;». A grocery delivery exemption has ended: «(p) subject to sub-paragraph (1A), bags intended to be used solely for the purpose of carrying goods purchased» and these bags were «exempted from the charge under regulation 6 only until midnight on [ F13 31 December 2020 ]».\n\n*Analytical inference:* the exemption for mail order dispatch and courier bags is the one closest to freight; the text does not define a courier bag, so its edge is a question for counsel. The grocery delivery exemption ended at midnight on 31 December 2020, so it is a past date and no longer gives relief. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given bag falls within the courier-bag exemption.\n\n## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline\n\n- 30 November 2010: Regulations made («Made 30 November 2010»)\n- 1 October 2011: Regulations come into force in Wales («These Regulations apply in relation to Wales and come into force on 1 October 2011.»)\n- 31 May each year: a seller that meets both conditions publishes its record for the reporting year just ended («A seller must publish the record on or before 31 May in the reporting year following that to which the record relates.»)\n- 31 December 2020: the grocery delivery and collection bag exemption ended (past; «exempted from the charge under regulation 6 only until midnight on [ F13 31 December 2020 ]»)\n\n*Analytical inference:* the 31 May record date repeats each year for a seller; the 2020 date is a past step.\n\n## 15. Sources\n\n- The Single Use Carrier Bags Charge (Wales) Regulations 2010, Welsh Ministers, legislation.gov.uk: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/wsi/2010/2880\n",

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document\n\nThis document covers «Commission Decision of 15 September 1999 confirming the measures notified by Belgium pursuant to Article 6(6) of Directive 94/62/EC of the European Parliament and the Council on packaging and packaging waste», published as «Official Journal L 257 , 02/10/1999». It is a decision of the Commission, not a rule that sets duties on traders: it confirms measures that Belgium notified. Its addressee is stated in one sentence: «This Decision is addressed to the Kingdom of Belgium.» The text captured is the 1999 original. What the Decision says is quoted; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:*, and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.\n\n## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace\n\nThe Decision sits under a packaging directive that «aims to harmonise national measures concerning the management of packaging and packaging waste in order to prevent any impact thereof on the environment or to reduce such impact». Its operative rule is one article: «The measures notified by Belgium which exceed the maximum recovery and recycling target laid down respectively in Article 6(1)(a) and (b) of Directive 94/62/EC are hereby confirmed.»\n\nThe background is the Directive's recovery target: «Article 6(1)(a) establishes that, no later than 30 June 2001, between 50 % as a minimum and 65 % as a maximum by weight of the packaging waste will be recovered.» Article 6(6) lets a Member State go further: «Article 6(6) of Directive 94/62/EC allows Member States to go beyond targets set in Article 6(1)(a) and 6(1)(b) if the Member State provides to this effect appropriate capacities for recycling and recovery.» The Decision treats Belgium's higher rates as such a case, saying that «Belgium has asked for a derogation from Article 6(1)(a) and (b).»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the Decision changes nothing for a trader directly; it clears Belgium's higher packaging recovery and recycling targets, so the Belgian rules it describes in section 4 stay in place. The Decision names the duty-holders as economic operators, including importers; it names no freight business.\n\n## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action\n\nMONITORING: the Decision is addressed to Belgium alone and sets no step, cost or deadline on a freight business. The action is a check on packaged imports into Belgium.\n\n- A customs lead asks each Belgian consignee of filled packaging which party is the importer for the Belgian packaging take-back obligation described in section 4, and records the answer in the shipment file.\n- A compliance lead asks counsel whether the Belgian rules described in 1999 still apply in the same form and whether a forwarder can be treated as an importer.\n\n*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the Decision's description of the Belgian measures, whose duty falls on economic operators «This Cooperation Agreement sets out the obligation for economic operators (packaging fillers and users, including importers in case the packaging was filled outside Belgium) to takeback and recycle/recover the packaging materials contained in the packaging waste put on the market». *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business, or its customer, is the importer for a given consignment.\n\n## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain\n\nThe Decision names the Commission, the Member States, Belgium, the Interregional Commission for Packaging and economic operators. The Belgian duty it describes: «This Cooperation Agreement sets out the obligation for economic operators (packaging fillers and users, including importers in case the packaging was filled outside Belgium) to takeback and recycle/recover the packaging materials contained in the packaging waste put on the market». Operators may meet it «either individually or by contracting a third party», or be relieved by contract: «Economic operators can be relieved from the obligation to take back and recycle/recover packaging, by signing a contract with a». The Belgian measures do not turn on origin: «The Belgian measures apply without distinction to all packaging waste, whether arising from domestic or imported products.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a freight forwarder or carrier is not named. The importer of filled packaging is the role the text names that is closest to a freight business, and only where the packaging was filled outside Belgium. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder that clears or moves packaged goods into Belgium falls into the importer role.\n\n## 8. Substantive Requirements\n\nDecision. «The measures notified by Belgium which exceed the maximum recovery and recycling target laid down respectively in Article 6(1)(a) and (b) of Directive 94/62/EC are hereby confirmed.» «This Decision is addressed to the Kingdom of Belgium.»\n\nConditions. Belgium may exceed the Directive's targets if the measures are taken «on the condition that they avoid distortions of the internal market and do not hinder compliance by other Member States with the Directive.»\n\nWhat the confirmed Belgian measures require, as the Decision describes them. «This Cooperation Agreement sets out the obligation for economic operators (packaging fillers and users, including importers in case the packaging was filled outside Belgium) to takeback and recycle/recover the packaging materials contained in the packaging waste put on the market». Rates: «Its Article 3(2) sets out the following global minimum rates, by weight, of recycling and recovery of packaging waste: - for 1998: 45 % recycling - 70 % recovery - for 1999: 50 % recycling - 80 % recovery.» Operators report their plan: «Economic operators shall communicate to the Interregional Commission for Packaging how they intend to fulfil such an obligation.» The scope is wide: «The Belgian measures apply without distinction to all packaging waste, whether arising from domestic or imported products.» Waste moves under the Treaty's rules on goods: «Wastes are goods which fall under the scope of Articles 28 to 30 of the Treaty».\n\n*Analytical inference:* the Decision itself imposes no duty on a trader; the duties are those of the Belgian Cooperation Agreement that it confirms, and they fall on economic operators.\n\n*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Belgian Cooperation Agreement, as described in 1999, has changed since, and whether any of its duties reach a freight business.\n\nNo phase-in is stated in Articles 1 and 2.\n\nObligations surveyed: 4; workspace-adjacent: 2; extracted as FACT: 8.\n\n## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations\n\nThe Decision sets no registration or reporting duty on a trader. It describes the Belgian one: «Economic operators shall communicate to the Interregional Commission for Packaging how they intend to fulfil such an obligation.» The Belgian body then decides: «The Interregional Commission shall evaluate and, if appropriate, approve or refuse the way by which economic operators intend to fulfil their obligation».\n\n*Analytical inference:* what an importer must file and when is set in the Cooperation Agreement, whose text is not in the Decision beyond these lines, so the filing format and date are a gap that counsel or the Belgian body would fill.\n\n## 11. Operational System Requirements\n\nMONITORING: the Decision requires no system of a freight business. The Belgian operator can meet the take-back duty «either individually or by contracting a third party», so a customer may ask a forwarder for data on packaging; the Decision does not say what data. The tracking that follows is a gap, not a mandate.\n\n*Analytical inference:* this rests on the Belgian duty in section 4, which falls on the operator and importer. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a customer may ask a forwarder for packaging weights and material types for Belgian take-back.\n\n## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases\n\nThe edge of the Decision is its conditions and its relief. Belgium's targets may exceed the Directive's only «on the condition that they avoid distortions of the internal market and do not hinder compliance by other Member States with the Directive.». Operators may be relieved: «Economic operators can be relieved from the obligation to take back and recycle/recover packaging, by signing a contract with a».\n\n*Analytical inference:* an operator that signs with an agreed body is relieved of the take-back obligation itself, which narrows who bears it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given importer is covered by such a contract.\n\n## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline\n\n- 21 January 1997: the Belgian Cooperation Agreement adopted by decree in the three regions («a Decree of 21 January 1997 of the Flanders Region, a Decree of 16 January 1997 of the Walloon Region and an Ordinance of 24 January 1997 of the Brussels Region»)\n- 15 September 1999: Commission adopts the Decision («Done at Brussels, 15 September 1999.»)\n- 02/10/1999: published in the Official Journal («Official Journal L 257 , 02/10/1999»)\n- 30 June 2001: Directive recovery target date for Member States (past; «Article 6(1)(a) establishes that, no later than 30 June 2001, between 50 % as a minimum and 65 % as a maximum by weight of the packaging waste will be recovered.»)\n\n*Analytical inference:* the Decision states no date on which it enters into force and no deadline for a private party; the 2001 date is the Directive's target date for Member States.\n\n## 15. Sources\n\n- Commission Decision 1999/652/EC, Commission of the European Communities, EUR-Lex: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31999D0652\n",

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document\n\nThis document covers The Alternative Fuel Labelling and Greenhouse Gas Emissions (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2019, United Kingdom Statutory Instrument 2019 No. 421, with this heading: «The Alternative Fuel Labelling and Greenhouse Gas Emissions (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2019 Made 25th February 2019 Laid before Parliament 4th March 2019 Coming into force in accordance with regulation 1(2) to (4)». It sets labels for fuels and vehicles, so a driver can see which fuel a vehicle takes. Its reach: a relevant vehicle is one «(a) the manufacture of which is completed on or after 1st April 2020, (b) that can be fuelled with an alternative fuel at a refuelling point, and (c) that is placed on the market in the United Kingdom.» What the Regulations say is quoted; what that means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:*, and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.\n\n## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace\n\nThe Regulations carry out part of an EU directive: «Parts 1 to 3 of this instrument implement the requirements Article 7(1) and (2), and (4) to (6) of Directive 2014/94/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 October 2014 on the deployment of alternative fuels infrastructure». The purpose: «The purpose of Article 7 of the Directive is to standardise the labelling of types of motor vehicle fuel.» In plain terms, a refuelling point and a new vehicle must show which fuel it supplies or takes: «Part 2 places obligations on fuel retailers, from 1st September 2019, to label refuelling points in order to provide clear information to users about the alternative fuel they dispense.» Alternative fuel is defined broadly: it «means fuel or power sources which serve, at least partly, as a substitute for fossil oil sources in the energy supply to transport», and the list includes hydrogen, biofuels, natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas.    "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document\n\nThis document covers The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026, United Kingdom Statutory Instrument 2026 No. 701, with this heading: «The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026 Made 23rd June 2026 Laid before Parliament 1st July 2026 Coming into force 22nd July 2026». It changes the rules of an energy audit scheme for large companies. Its reach: «(3) These Regulations extend to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.» What the Regulations say is quoted; what that means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:*, and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.\n\n## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace\n\nThe Regulations change an earlier rule: «The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme Regulations 2014( 2 ) are amended in accordance with the following provisions.» The Explanatory Note says: «These Regulations make changes in relation to the Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme». The scheme asks a large company to audit its energy use and report on it.\n\nThree changes matter most. First, a company that holds a certified energy management system is treated as having complied: «they are deemed to have complied with the duty to appoint a lead assessor, carry out an ESOS audit and produce an ESOS report.» Second, a company with no energy use is excused: «An additional route for compliance is inserted for undertakings whose energy consumption is zero kWh.» «Those undertakings are exempt from the requirement to complete an ESOS assessment, as well as the duties under Chapters 2A to 4 of Part 4 and Part 6A of the 2014 Regulations.» Third, new steps are added: «Subject to paragraph (3), when carrying out an ESOS assessment in accordance with Chapter 1 of this Part, a responsible undertaking must also produce an estimate of energy savings achieved by the participant in that compliance period, in kWh.» and «Subject to paragraph (3), when conducting an ESOS assessment in accordance with Chapter 1 of this Part, a responsible undertaking must also complete an ESOS action plan review.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a freight business is affected if it is a large company in the scheme, because the audit and report duties change; the text names no freight operator. The Government expects little cost: «A full impact assessment has not been produced for this instrument as no, or no significant impact on the private, voluntary or public sectors is foreseen.»\n\n## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action\n\nMONITORING: the Regulations came into force on 22nd July 2026 and the next dated step is 5th December 2027, so no step falls due in the next 30 days. The action is a plan for the first compliance period that ends on or after that date.\n\n- A compliance lead lists the business's compliance periods and marks any that ends on or after 5th December 2027, because the final progress update and a new reporting rule start there.\n- An energy manager checks how much of the business's energy use falls under a certified ISO 50001 system, since significant energy consumption means the areas of use that make up 95% or more of the total.\n\n*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on regulations 28 and 33 as amended. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is in the scheme and which compliance period it is now in.\n\n## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain\n\nThe Regulations name the responsible undertaking, the participant, the lead assessor, the approval body, the scheme administrator and the Secretary of State. A new duty falls on the lead assessor: «Within the period of seven days beginning with the day after the day on which a notification is made under paragraph (2)(b), the lead assessor must» «(a) notify their approval body of the completion of the ESOS assessment, including the date of completion;»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a freight forwarder or carrier is not named. A freight company that is a responsible undertaking carries the audit, estimate and action plan review duties; its lead assessor carries the notification. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is a responsible undertaking, and which entity in a group holds the role.\n\n## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events\n\nOne dated step is ahead: «for compliance periods ending on or after 5th December 2027, an ESOS progress update during the period starting on the three year anniversary of the first day of the relevant compliance period and ending on the day before the four year anniversary of the first day of the relevant compliance period».\n\n*Analytical inference:* the step applies to compliance periods that end on or after 5th December 2027, so a business with an earlier ending period is not yet in it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the end date of the business's current compliance period.\n\n## 8. Substantive Requirements\n\nSavings estimate. «Subject to paragraph (3), when carrying out an ESOS assessment in accordance with Chapter 1 of this Part, a responsible undertaking must also produce an estimate of energy savings achieved by the participant in that compliance period, in kWh.»\n\nAction plan review. «Subject to paragraph (3), when conducting an ESOS assessment in accordance with Chapter 1 of this Part, a responsible undertaking must also complete an ESOS action plan review.» The review records why measures were not carried out: «(b) an explanation of the reasons why those measures were not implemented,»\n\nLead assessor. «Within the period of seven days beginning with the day after the day on which a notification is made under paragraph (2)(b), the lead assessor must» «(a) notify their approval body of the completion of the ESOS assessment, including the date of completion;»\n\nUnits. «This Chapter is also amended to require all estimates of energy consumption or energy savings to be calculated in kWh.»\n\nEvidence. The evidence a participant keeps now covers «(vi) the preparation of any ESOS report under regulation 27A, (vii) the calculation of estimated energy savings since the previous compliance date under regulation 27D, (viii) any ESOS action plan under regulation 34A, (ix) any ESOS progress update under regulation 34B,»\n\nFinal progress update and reporting. «for compliance periods ending on or after 5th December 2027, an ESOS progress update during the period starting on the three year anniversary of the first day of the relevant compliance period and ending on the day before the four year anniversary of the first day of the relevant compliance period». «(b) an ESOS assessment carried out for a compliance period ending on or after 5th December 2027, where the participant is deemed to have complied with this Chapter in accordance with regulation 33(3) or 33A.»\n\nExclusions. «Chapter 1 of Part 3 of the 2014 Regulations is amended to expand the exclusion for insolvent undertakings to include any undertakings subject to insolvency proceedings during the period starting with the qualification date and ending with the compliance date.» «Part 6 of the 2014 Regulations is amended to remove Display Energy Certificates and Green Deal Assessments as alternative routes to compliance.» No energy use: «Those undertakings are exempt from the requirement to complete an ESOS assessment, as well as the duties under Chapters 2A to 4 of Part 4 and Part 6A of the 2014 Regulations.»\n\nLimits. «This regulation does not apply to a participant which is deemed to have complied with this Chapter by virtue of regulation 33A.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the new duties add estimates, a review and a notification to an audit scheme the company already runs; the text states no price or penalty and the impact note foresees no significant impact. No phase-in is stated in Sections 27D and 27E of the inserted chapter beyond the date in the progress update rule.\n\n*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is a participant and which of the new duties applies to it. No penalty amount is stated in this text.\n\nObligations surveyed: 6; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 12.\n\n## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations\n\nInformation goes to the scheme administrator by notification. The tables in the amended Schedule say what is notified and published, for example the energy savings estimate: «to be notified to the scheme administrator under regulation 29». The lead assessor must tell the approval body when an assessment is complete: «(a) notify their approval body of the completion of the ESOS assessment, including the date of completion;»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the new tables extend what a participant must notify; the text names no registration fee. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which table entries apply to the business and which are published.\n\n## 11. Operational System Requirements\n\nMONITORING: the Regulations require a business in the scheme to produce data in a set form. Estimates are in kilowatt hours: «This Chapter is also amended to require all estimates of energy consumption or energy savings to be calculated in kWh.» And more records are kept: «(vi) the preparation of any ESOS report under regulation 27A, (vii) the calculation of estimated energy savings since the previous compliance date under regulation 27D, (viii) any ESOS action plan under regulation 34A, (ix) any ESOS progress update under regulation 34B,»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a business that metered energy in other units needs the kWh conversion and a record of the estimate data. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which records the business must retain for each new duty.\n\n## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases\n\nFour edges are stated. A certified system: «they are deemed to have complied with the duty to appoint a lead assessor, carry out an ESOS audit and produce an ESOS report.» The line for it: «the areas of energy consumption comprising 95% or more of that participant». A business with no energy use: «Those undertakings are exempt from the requirement to complete an ESOS assessment, as well as the duties under Chapters 2A to 4 of Part 4 and Part 6A of the 2014 Regulations.» An insolvent company: «Chapter 1 of Part 3 of the 2014 Regulations is amended to expand the exclusion for insolvent undertakings to include any undertakings subject to insolvency proceedings during the period starting with the qualification date and ending with the compliance date.» The new chapter does not apply to those deemed compliant: «This regulation does not apply to a participant which is deemed to have complied with this Chapter by virtue of regulation 33A.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* deemed compliance means a business covered by a certified system needs less work, but it still notifies the information in the tables for deemed compliance. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given group company meets the insolvency exclusion.\n\n## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline\n\n- 23rd June 2026: Regulations made («Made 23rd June 2026»)\n- 1st July 2026: laid before Parliament («Laid before Parliament 1st July 2026»)\n- 22nd July 2026: Regulations in force («(2) These Regulations come into force on 22nd July 2026.»)\n- 5th December 2027: the final progress update and the new reporting rule apply to compliance periods ending on or after this date («(b) an ESOS assessment carried out for a compliance period ending on or after 5th December 2027, where the participant is deemed to have complied with this Chapter in accordance with regulation 33(3) or 33A.»)\n\n*Analytical inference:* the first three dates are past; 5th December 2027 is the one step ahead.\n\n## 15. Sources\n\n- The Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2026, Secretary of State, legislation.gov.uk: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/701\n",

Purpose and Scope of This Document\n\nThis document covers «COMMISSION REGULATION (EU) 2024/2462 of 19 September 2024 amending Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards undecafluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA), its salts and PFHxA-related substances». It adds an entry to the list of restricted chemicals in the EU's chemicals rule. Its reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» Its operative text is one article: «Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation.» What the Regulation says is quoted; what that means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:*, and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.\n\n## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace\n\nThe Regulation restricts PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances. The Commission found a risk: «an unacceptable risk to human health and the environment arises from the use and placing on the market of PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances in certain mixtures and in certain articles, which needs to be addressed on a Union-wide basis.» The uses are wide: «PFHxA-related substances and the ammonium salt of PFHxA are widely used in many sectors, with large quantities used in paper and cardboard for use as food contact materials, in textiles and in firefighting foams.»\n\nThe restriction bans, above set limits, the placing on the market or use of PFHxA, its salts and related substances in listed goods, in stages. The goods are consumer clothing and accessories, footwear, food-contact paper and board, mixtures and cosmetics. A later stage covers other textiles: «The product types concerned include carpets, rugs, curtains, blinds, upholstery, textile wall covers and other textile-based coverings (such as tablecloths or bed linen).» The Commission adds: «That includes product types concerned in transport and public places, as well as in offices as it can be assumed that those offices are visited by the general public.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a freight business is touched when it moves these goods for the general public into the EU for sale. Freight moved before sale does not fall into a role the text names, but the customer who places the goods on the market does, so the effect reaches a forwarder through customer questions and held cargo, and the text states no cost or surcharge.\n\n## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action\n\nWINDOW CLOSING: the restriction has started for some goods and the transition for the next group closes on 10 October 2027. Textiles other than clothing for the general public, such as carpets, curtains and upholstery, are the next stage; firefighting foam for civil aviation closes on 10 October 2029.\n\n- A trade compliance lead writes to each customer that ships clothing, footwear, food-contact paper or board, cosmetics or consumer mixtures into the EU and asks for written confirmation that the goods meet the limits of 25 ppb and 1 000 ppb, for goods placed on the market from 10 October 2026.\n- A key account lead asks customers shipping carpets, curtains, upholstery and similar textiles for the general public to confirm their supply plan before 10 October 2027, and notes that earlier-placed articles are carved out.\n- An aviation cargo lead asks any customer that supplies firefighting foam to a civil airport for its plan for 10 October 2029.\n\n*Analytical inference:* each step rests on paragraphs 1, 2 and 5 of the entry, which bar placing on the market or use in the goods listed. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business, or its customer, is the party that places a given consignment on the market.\n\n## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain\n\nThe Regulation names the Commission, Member States, the Agency, suppliers, public fire services, and producers, importers and users of substances. The supplier role: «The restriction should not apply to articles and mixtures for which the supplier can demonstrate that such articles and mixtures were placed on the market prior to the respective date of application of the restriction, for practicality and enforceability reasons.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a freight forwarder or carrier is not named. The nearest roles are the supplier and the importer of the goods; the entry says the goods shall not be placed on the market, so the duty is on whoever places them and not on a party that moves them. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder that acts as importer of record is a party that places goods on the market.\n\n## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events\n\nTwo wider restriction files are still open: «uses of PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances not covered by this targeted restriction, are also included in two other pending restriction dossiers, notably PFAS in firefighting foams ( 11 ) and PFAS in all other uses ( 12 ) .» The Commission says what follows: «The Commission will further consider the need to restrict those uses based on the justification and information provided in those dossiers and the related opinions.» Foam is the overlap: the Agency's dossier proposes «proposing to restrict the manufacture, placing on the market and use of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in firefighting foams».\n\n*Analytical inference:* the uses this entry leaves out, including other firefighting foam uses, may be restricted later through those files; the text gives no date for a decision. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the status of those two files.\n\n## 7. Threshold Questions\n\nWhether a good is caught turns on the substance: «PFHxA-related substances are substances that, based on their molecular structure, are considered to have the potential to degrade or be transformed to PFHxA.» It also turns on what is excluded: «(c) any substance having a perfluoroalkyl group C 6 F 13 - directly attached to an oxygen atom at one of the non-terminal carbon atoms.» And on who buys: the list is for the general public.\n\n*Analytical inference:* a good that is caught is one that contains the listed substances above the limits in the listed goods, so a test result, not the label, is what decides. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which substances in a given consignment are PFHxA-related.\n\n## 8. Substantive Requirements\n\nClothing, footwear, food-contact paper, consumer mixtures and cosmetics. «Shall not, from 10 October 2026 be placed on the market, or used, in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances, measured in homogeneous material, in the following:» «(a) textiles, leather, furs and hides in clothing and related accessories for the general public; (b) footwear for the general public; (c) paper and cardboard used as food contact materials within the scope of Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004; (d) mixtures for the general public; (e) cosmetic products as defined in Article 2(1), point (a), of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009.»\n\nOther textiles. «Shall not, from 10 October 2027 be placed on the market, or used, in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances, measured in homogeneous material, in textiles, leather, furs and hides, other than in clothing and related accessories referred to in paragraph 1, for the general public.»\n\nFirefighting foam, training, testing and public fire services. «Shall not, from 10 April 2026 be placed on the market, or used, in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances, in: (a) firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates for training and for testing, except functional testing of the firefighting systems provided that all releases are contained;» «(b) firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates for public fire services, except where those services intervene at industrial fires at establishments covered by Directive 2012/18/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ( *1 ) and they use the foams and the equipment for that purpose only.»\n\nCivil aviation foam. «Shall not, from 10 October 2029 be placed on the market, or used, in firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates for civil aviation (including in civilian airports) in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances.»\n\nCarve-outs. «Paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not apply to the following: (a) personal protective equipment intended to protect users against risks within the scope of risk category III, points (a), (c) to (f), (h), and (l) of Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2016/425; (b) devices within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2017/745; (c) devices within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2017/746; (d) textiles used as construction textiles.» «By way of derogation from paragraph 1, that paragraph shall not apply to articles and mixtures which were placed on the market before 10 October 2026.» «By way of derogation from paragraph 2, that paragraph shall not apply to articles which were placed on the market before 10 October 2027.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the limits are 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts and 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances, tested in homogeneous material; the stages are 10 April 2026, 10 October 2026, 10 October 2027 and 10 October 2029, and the text states no price or surcharge.\n\n*Legal Confirmation Required:* which stage and limit apply to a given good, and whether the Article 1 amendment of REACH reaches the business as a supplier or importer. No penalty is stated in this text.\n\nObligations surveyed: 6; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 9.\n\n## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations\n\nThe entry sets no registration or reporting duty on a trader. The recitals record a proposal that the final text did not adopt as an entry duty: «For the use of PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances in firefighting foams, Germany proposed a reporting obligation for a natural or legal person benefitting from the proposed derogations.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the adopted entry text in the Annex carries no reporting duty for firefighting foams, so a business needs no filing under it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any reporting duty applies under other provisions of the chemicals rule.\n\n## 11. Operational System Requirements\n\nWINDOW CLOSING: a supplier may show that goods were placed on the market before a date, as section 4 quotes. Two derogations follow: «By way of derogation from paragraph 1, that paragraph shall not apply to articles and mixtures which were placed on the market before 10 October 2026.» and «By way of derogation from paragraph 2, that paragraph shall not apply to articles which were placed on the market before 10 October 2027.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a business that holds goods over a date needs a record of when each lot was placed on the market, and a test report for the limits; the text does not say what proof is accepted. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the proof a supplier needs to show placing before 10 October 2026 or 10 October 2027.\n\n## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases\n\nPersonal protective equipment, listed medical devices and construction textiles are carved out of paragraphs 1 and 2 by paragraph 3. Public fire services have an edge in paragraph 4: «(b) firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates for public fire services, except where those services intervene at industrial fires at establishments covered by Directive 2012/18/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ( *1 ) and they use the foams and the equipment for that purpose only.» Articles placed on the market earlier are outside: «By way of derogation from paragraph 1, that paragraph shall not apply to articles and mixtures which were placed on the market before 10 October 2026.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the stock carve-out lets existing stock run, but only for goods placed on the market before the stage date, so a later import of the same goods is caught. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given product is personal protective equipment or a device within the listed Regulations.\n\n## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives\n\nThe Commission rests the foam timing on available alternatives: «given that alternatives are widely available and already in use to replace PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances in firefighting foams used for training and testing, for public fire services and for civil aviation, the Commission considers that restricting those uses should not be delayed.» The expert committees' views are recorded: «RAC considers that a broad Union-wide restriction with carefully considered targeted derogations and transition periods is the most appropriate Union-wide measure to address the identified risks in terms of effectiveness, practicality and monitorability.» and «SEAC considered that a restriction on PFHxA, its salts and PFHxA-related substances is, in general, an appropriate measure to address the identified risks.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the record shows alternatives exist for the foam uses restricted first and that the committees backed a restriction in general; it does not name a product or supplier.\n\n## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline\n\n- 19 September 2024: Commission adopts the Regulation («Done at Brussels, 19 September 2024.»)\n- 10 April 2026: firefighting foam for training, testing and public fire services restricted (past; «Shall not, from 10 April 2026 be placed on the market, or used, in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances, in: (a) firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates for training and for testing, except functional testing of the firefighting systems provided that all releases are contained;»)\n- 10 October 2026: clothing, footwear, food-contact paper and board, consumer mixtures and cosmetics restricted (in effect; «Shall not, from 10 October 2026 be placed on the market, or used, in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances, measured in homogeneous material, in the following:»)\n- 10 October 2027: other textiles for the general public restricted («Shall not, from 10 October 2027 be placed on the market, or used, in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances, measured in homogeneous material, in textiles, leather, furs and hides, other than in clothing and related accessories referred to in paragraph 1, for the general public.»)\n- 10 October 2029: firefighting foam for civil aviation restricted («Shall not, from 10 October 2029 be placed on the market, or used, in firefighting foams and firefighting foam concentrates for civil aviation (including in civilian airports) in a concentration equal to or greater than 25 ppb for the sum of PFHxA and its salts, or 1 000 ppb for the sum of PFHxA-related substances.»)\n\n*Analytical inference:* the 10 April 2026 and 10 October 2026 stages have passed and are in effect; 10 October 2027 and 10 October 2029 are ahead. The Regulation enters into force as the text states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union».\n\n## 15. Sources\n\n- Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462, European Commission, EUR-Lex: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R2462\n",

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document\n\nThis document covers a Norwegian rule, not an EU one: «Circular - Series R Number: RSR 04-2025 Date: 14.04.2025 Case number: 2024/72534 Adoption of zero-emission requirements for cruise ships, tourist boats and ferries in the World Heritage fjords». The stored title, Norway Zero-Emission Shipping, names no single instrument; the captures hold the circular, a Government news story, a Maritime Authority news story and consultation page, a Lloyd's Register note and two other news items.    "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document\n\nThis document covers «COMMISSION REGULATION (EU) No 412/2012 of 15 May 2012 amending Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council on the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH)». It adds a chemical to the EU's list of restricted substances in articles. Its reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» Its operative text is one article: «Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation.» What the Regulation says is quoted; what that means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:*, and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.\n\n## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace\n\nThe Regulation targets one substance, dimethylfumarate (DMF). The Commission records the risk: «DMF contained in articles or parts thereof, in concentrations greater than 0,1 mg/kg, poses a risk to human health». The harm was seen in goods on sale: «Furniture and footwear available on the market in several Member States have been identified as the cause of damage to the health of consumers in France, Poland, Finland, Sweden and the United Kingdom.» The link to cargo is in the recital on how it was used: «DMF, which is a biocide that prevents moulds that may deteriorate leather furniture or footwear during storage or transport in a humid climate. DMF was most often contained in little pouches fixed inside the furniture or added to the footwear boxes.» The injury: «DMF came into contact with consumers’ skin where it caused a number of cases of sensitisation (contact dermatitis), resulting in a painful condition.»\n\nThe gap it closes: «Directive 98/8/EC does not foresee restricting the import into the Union of articles treated with biocides.» Before this Regulation an emergency measure applied, and the recital records that «Commission has adopted Decision 2009/251/EC of 17 March 2009 requiring Member States to ensure that products containing the biocide dimethylfumarate are not placed or made available on the market», and that this earlier ban «is applicable until the entry into force of this Regulation or 15 March 2013, whichever is the earlier.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the freight link is the pouch or box sachet put inside shipments of leather furniture and footwear to stop mould on long humid transport; the Regulation bars the finished article from the market above the limit, and does not name a carrier or forwarder.\n\n## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action\n\nMONITORING: the Regulation sets no dated step now, but it bars articles with DMF above 0,1 mg/kg from the market, and its recitals name leather furniture and footwear in transit as the source. The check is on those cargo types.\n\n- A cargo lead asks each shipper of leather furniture or footwear into the EU whether the goods or boxes carry anti-mould sachets and whether DMF is the agent, before the shipment is accepted.\n- A claims lead keeps the shipper's written answer in the shipment file.\n\n*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the entry's limit and the recital on pouches in boxes. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder that handles such a consignment is a party that places articles on the market.\n\n## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain\n\nThe Regulation names the Commission, the Agency, Member States, consumers and, in the entry, the person who uses DMF in articles or places articles on the market. It does not say who that person is: «61. Dimethylfumarate (DMF) CAS No 624-49-7 EC 210-849-0 Shall not be used in articles or any parts thereof in concentrations greater than 0,1 mg/kg. Articles or any parts thereof containing DMF in concentrations greater than 0,1 mg/kg shall not be placed on the market.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a freight forwarder or carrier is not named. The duty is on use in articles and on placing on the market, so the shipper or importer is the party the wording points to; a forwarder moving the goods is not described. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder acting as importer is a party that places the articles on the market.\n\n## 8. Substantive Requirements\n\nEntry 61. «61. Dimethylfumarate (DMF) CAS No 624-49-7 EC 210-849-0 Shall not be used in articles or any parts thereof in concentrations greater than 0,1 mg/kg. Articles or any parts thereof containing DMF in concentrations greater than 0,1 mg/kg shall not be placed on the market.»\n\nWhy a limit by concentration. «DMF contained in articles or parts thereof, in concentrations greater than 0,1 mg/kg, poses a risk to human health».\n\n*Analytical inference:* the limit is 0,1 mg/kg in the article or any part of it, so a sachet or a treated lining inside a larger article is measured by its own concentration; the text states no price or surcharge.\n\n*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given product contains DMF above the limit and which party is liable. No penalty is stated in this text.\n\nNo phase-in is stated in Articles 1 and 2. No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 and 2 or in entry 61. No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2.\n\nObligations surveyed: 2; workspace-adjacent: 1; extracted as FACT: 2.\n\n## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations\n\nThe Regulation sets no registration or reporting duty on a trader. The entry is a ban on use and on placing on the market: «61. Dimethylfumarate (DMF) CAS No 624-49-7 EC 210-849-0 Shall not be used in articles or any parts thereof in concentrations greater than 0,1 mg/kg. Articles or any parts thereof containing DMF in concentrations greater than 0,1 mg/kg shall not be placed on the market.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a business has no filing under this entry; the entry bars use in articles and placing articles on the market above the limit; it does not mention carriage. *Legal Confirmation Required:* any duty under other provisions of the chemicals rule.\n\n## 11. Operational System Requirements\n\nMONITORING: the text requires no system. The operational step that follows is a pre-shipment question at acceptance on anti-mould agents for leather furniture and footwear, as the recital on pouches in boxes explains.\n\n*Analytical inference:* a business that handles these cargoes needs an intake field or checklist line for anti-mould agents; the text does not say what proof is accepted. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the proof of absence of DMF a shipper must give.\n\n## 14.    "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document\n\nThis document covers The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022, United Kingdom Statutory Instrument 2022 No. 454, with this heading: «The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2022 Made 13th April 2022 Coming into force 14th April 2022». It changes the enforcement rules of the United Kingdom's carbon allowance scheme. Its reach: «This Order extends to the whole of the United Kingdom.» What the Order says is quoted; what that means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:*, and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.\n\n## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace\n\nThe Order changes an earlier Order: «The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Order 2020( 2 ) is amended in accordance with this Part.» The Explanatory Note describes the scheme: «Operators of certain industrial installations and certain aircraft operators are required to monitor, report on, and surrender “allowances” equivalent to, their greenhouse gas emissions in each scheme year.»\n\nThe changes are about enforcement. Inspections: «The power to inspect premises to ensure compliance may be exercised by an “authorised person” as well as the regulator (see amendment to article 39 of the UK ETS Order).» Obstruction: «It is an offence to intentionally obstruct persons in the exercise of the enforcement powers referred to in article 40(1) (see amendments to article 40).» Allowances: «Persons who fail to comply with a notice to return allowances under article 34V may be subject to a civil penalty (see amendments to article 47 and new article 64A).» Re-made rules: «The effect of articles 7, 11, 12 and 14 of this Order is that the amendments made by the 2020 Amendment Order are revoked and are re-made by this Order, which is subject to the affirmative resolution procedure.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the part of the scheme nearest to freight is the aircraft operators the Note names; the Order puts its duties on operators and persons who receive notices, and the text names no forwarder or shipper. It states no pass-through of any allowance cost to a customer.\n\n## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action\n\nMONITORING: the Order came into force on 14th April 2022, so no step is due now. The practical question for a freight business is whether an air carrier it uses is exposed to the new penalty and how the carrier prices that exposure.\n\n- A carrier-relations lead asks each air carrier in its rate agreements whether it is an aircraft operator under the scheme and whether any allowance cost is added to rates and how it is calculated.\n- A compliance lead asks counsel whether the business operates any installation or aircraft that the scheme covers.\n\n*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the Note's description of the scheme and on article 64A below; the text states no pass-through. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any entity of the business is an operator within the scheme.\n\n## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain\n\nThe Order names the regulator, an authorised person, the registry administrator, operators of installations, aircraft operators and any person who gets a notice to return allowances. The registry administrator gains a notice power: «Where the registry administrator considers that a person has contravened, is contravening or is likely to contravene a requirement imposed on the person by or under Schedule 5A, the registry administrator may give notice»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a freight forwarder or carrier is not named as such; an air carrier that is an aircraft operator falls under the scheme's operator duties. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which role a given air carrier or group company holds.\n\n## 8. Substantive Requirements\n\nPenalty for not returning allowances. «A person is liable to a civil penalty where the person fails to comply (or to comply on time) with the requirements of a notice (the “notice to return allowances”) given under article 34V.» The amount: «(a) £20,000; and (b) a daily penalty at a daily rate of £1,000 for each day that the person fails to comply with the requirements of the notice to return allowances, beginning with the day on which the initial notice is given.» The daily part has no cap: «A penalty notice imposing a civil penalty that consists of a daily penalty under article 64A(2)(b) (for which there is no maximum) may be given at such intervals as the regulator considers appropriate.»\n\nPermit surrender and revocation. «Where an installation’s permit is surrendered or revoked, the surrender or revocation notice given will include a requirement to surrender any deficit of allowances from previous scheme years (see amendments to paragraphs 11 and 12 of Schedule 6).»\n\nEnforcement powers. «The power to inspect premises to ensure compliance may be exercised by an “authorised person” as well as the regulator (see amendment to article 39 of the UK ETS Order).» «It is an offence to intentionally obstruct persons in the exercise of the enforcement powers referred to in article 40(1) (see amendments to article 40).» The registry administrator may also give an enforcement notice: «Where the registry administrator considers that a person has contravened, is contravening or is likely to contravene a requirement imposed on the person by or under Schedule 5A, the registry administrator may give notice», and an earlier carve-out in article 44: «after “this Order” insert “, except for Schedule 5A”».\n\nCure of a doubt. «The effect of articles 7, 11, 12 and 14 of this Order is that the amendments made by the 2020 Amendment Order are revoked and are re-made by this Order, which is subject to the affirmative resolution procedure.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the penalty is a flat amount plus a daily amount that runs until the notice is met, so exposure grows each day of delay; it falls on the person who gets the notice, not on a customer. No phase-in is stated in Articles 4 to 14 of this Order. No scope limits are stated in Articles 4 to 14 of this Order beyond its extent in article 3.\n\n*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business or a carrier it uses is a person who could receive a notice to return allowances.\n\nObligations surveyed: 5; workspace-adjacent: 1; extracted as FACT: 9.\n\n## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations\n\nThe Order sets no new registration. The reporting and surrender duty it builds on is in the scheme: «Operators of certain industrial installations and certain aircraft operators are required to monitor, report on, and surrender “allowances” equivalent to, their greenhouse gas emissions in each scheme year.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the Order leaves that duty with operators, and adds penalties when a notice to return allowances is not met. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the form and date of each notice, which each notice sets.\n\n## 11. Operational System Requirements\n\nMONITORING: the Order requires no system of a freight business. An operator in the scheme must allow inspection: «The power to inspect premises to ensure compliance may be exercised by an “authorised person” as well as the regulator (see amendment to article 39 of the UK ETS Order).»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a business that is an operator needs a named contact for an authorised person's visit and a way to track a notice and its date, because the daily penalty runs from the day the initial notice is given. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is an operator at all.\n\n## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases\n\nOne edge is stated: «The operator will not be subject to a second “excess emissions penalty” in respect of any failure to comply with this requirement (see amendments to article 52).»\n\n*Analytical inference:* an operator that fails to meet the permit surrender requirement is not penalised twice for the same failure under article 52. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether that protection reaches the penalty in article 64A.\n\n## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline\n\n- 13th April 2022: Order made («Made 13th April 2022»)\n- 14th April 2022: Order comes into force («Coming into force 14th April 2022»)\n\n*Analytical inference:* both dates are past; the Order, which enters into force on 14th April 2022 as its heading states, is in effect; it states that «This Order comes into force on the day after the day on which it is made.» and sets no later dated step for a private party.\n\n## 15.
