     "slot_key": null
    },
    {
     "section": "1",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "The Regulation should ensure a high level of protection of human health and the environment and the free movement of chemical substances, mixtures and certain articles.",
     "source_span": "(1) This Regulation should ensure a high level of protection of human health and the environment as well as the free movement of chemical substances, mixtures and certain specific articles, while enhancing competitiveness and innovation.",
     "source_url": "https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272",
     "slot_key": null
    },
    {
     "section": "1",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "Manufacturers, importers and downstream users must classify substances and mixtures placed on the market, and suppliers must label and package them.",
     "source_span": "(b) providing an obligation for: (i) manufacturers, importers and downstream users to classify substances and mixtures placed on the market; (ii) suppliers to label and package substances and mixtures placed on the market;",
     "source_url": "https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272",
     "slot_key": null
    },
    {
     "section": "1",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "[jurisdictional_scope] This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.",
     "source_span": "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.",
     "source_url": "https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272",
     "slot_key": "jurisdictional_scope"
    },
    {
     "section": "2",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "A supplier is any manufacturer, importer, downstream user or distributor placing on the market a substance or a mixture.",
     "source_span": "\"supplier\" means any manufacturer, importer, downstream user or distributor placing on the market a substance, on its own or in a mixture, or a mixture;",
     "source_url": "https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272",
     "slot_key": null
    },
    {
     "section": "2",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "Placing on the market means supplying or making available to a third party, and import is deemed to be placing on the market.",
     "source_span": "\"placing on the market\" means supplying or making available, whether in return for payment or free of charge, to a third party. Import shall be deemed to be placing on the market;",
     "source_url": "https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272",
     "slot_key": null
    },
    {
     "section": "2",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "[effective_date] This Regulation enters into force on the 20th day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.",
     "source_span": "This Regulation shall enter into force on the 20th day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.",
     "source_url": "https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272",
     "slot_key": "effective_date"
    },
    {
     "section": "2",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "[primary_deadline] Titles II, III and IV apply in respect of substances from 1 December 2010 and in respect of mixtures from 1 June 2015.",
     "source_span": "Titles II, III and IV shall apply in respect of substances from 1 December 2010 and in respect of mixtures from 1 June 2015.",
     "source_url": "https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272",
     "slot_key": "primary_deadline"
    },
    {
     "section": "4",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "An importer is any natural or legal person established within the Community who is responsible for import.",
     "source_span": "\"importer\" means any natural or legal person established within the Community who is responsible for import;",
     "source_url": "https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272",
     "slot_key": null
    },
    {
     "section": "4",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "Import is the physical introduction into the customs territory of the Community.",
     "source_span": "\"import\" means the physical introduction into the customs territory of the Community;",

     "slot_key": null
    },
    {
     "section": "4",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "A distributor is any person established within the Community, including a retailer, who only stores and places on the market a substance or mixture for third parties.",
     "source_span": "\"distributor\" means any natural or legal person established within the Community, including a retailer, who only stores and places on the market a substance, on its own or in a mixture, for third parties;",

     "slot_key": null
    },
    {
     "section": "4",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "Suppliers in a supply chain shall cooperate to meet the classification, labelling and packaging requirements.",
     "source_span": "Suppliers in a supply chain shall cooperate to meet the requirements for classification, labelling and packaging in this Regulation.",
     "source_url": "https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272",
     "slot_key": null
    },

     "section": "7",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "Save where Article 33 applies, the Regulation shall not apply to the transport of dangerous goods by air, sea, road, rail or inland waterways.",
     "source_span": "Save where Article 33 applies this Regulation shall not apply to the transport of dangerous goods by air, sea, road, rail or inland waterways.",

     "slot_key": null
    },
    {
     "section": "7",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "Where the outer package meets the transport dangerous goods labelling rules, the inner and any intermediate packaging shall be labelled in accordance with this Regulation.",
     "source_span": "Where a package consists of an outer and an inner packaging, together with any intermediate packaging, and the outer packaging meets labelling provisions in accordance with the rules on the transport of dangerous goods, the inner and any intermediate packaging shall be labelled in accordance with this Regulation.",

     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "Where the outer package is not required to meet the transport labelling rules, both the outer and any inner packaging shall be labelled in accordance with this Regulation, unless the outer packaging lets the inner label be clearly seen.",
     "source_span": "Where the outer packaging of a package is not required to meet labelling provisions in accordance with rules on the transport of dangerous goods, both the outer and any inner packaging, including any intermediate packaging, shall be labelled in accordance with this Regulation.     {
     "section": "8",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "Manufacturers, importers and downstream users shall classify substances or mixtures before placing them on the market.",
     "source_span": "Manufacturers, importers and downstream users shall classify substances or mixtures in accordance with Title II before placing them on the market.",
     "source_url": "https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272",
     "slot_key": null

    {
     "section": "8",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "Where a substance or mixture is classified as hazardous, suppliers shall ensure it is labelled and packaged in accordance with Titles III and IV before placing it on the market.",
     "source_span": "Where a substance or mixture is classified as hazardous, suppliers shall ensure that the substance or mixture is labelled and packaged in accordance with Titles III and IV, before placing it on the market.",

    },
    {

     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "Substances and mixtures shall not be placed on the market unless they comply with this Regulation.",

     "source_url": "https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32008R1272",
     "slot_key": null
    },
    {
     "section": "8",
     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "A hazardous substance or mixture in packaging shall bear a label including the supplier's name, address and telephone number and other listed elements.",
     "source_span": "A substance or mixture classified as hazardous and contained in packaging shall bear a label including the following elements: (a) the name, address and telephone number of the supplier(s);",

     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "The label shall be written in the official language(s) of the Member State(s) where the substance or mixture is placed on the market, unless the Member State provides otherwise.",
     "source_span": "The label shall be written in the official language(s) of the Member State(s) where the substance or mixture is placed on the market, unless the Member State(s) concerned provide(s) otherwise.",

     "claim_kind": "FACT",
     "claim_text": "The Regulation shall not apply to radioactive substances and mixtures within the scope of Council Directive 96/29/Euratom of 13 May 1996.",

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document\n\nThis document covers New York City Local Law 97 of 2019 (LL97), the city's cap on greenhouse gas emissions from large buildings, with its penalty rule. The Department of Buildings (DOB) describes the cap: «Under this groundbreaking law, most buildings over 25,000 square feet are required to meet new GHG emissions limits beginning in 2024, with stricter limits coming into effect in 2030.» And the aim: reducing emissions of the largest buildings by «40 percent by 2030 and to net zero by 2050». The rule on penalties is recorded on the city rules portal: «The Department of Buildings (“DOB” or “Department”) is amending section 103-14 to establish penalties for noncompliance with Article 320 of Chapter 3 of Title 28 of the New York City Administrative Code requiring annual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions limits for buildings and to establish a credit for beneficial electrification.» The jurisdiction is New York City. Which buildings are covered: «LL97 covers: a building that exceeds 25,000 gross square feet two or more buildings on the same tax lot that together exceed 50,000 gross square feet two or more condominium buildings governed by the same board of managers and that together exceed 50,000 gross square feet.» What the texts say is stated from their own wording; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.\n\n## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace\n\nLL97 limits the carbon dioxide equivalent a building may emit each year, by the use of its floor area. The regulation enters into force for covered buildings on the date it sets: «Except as otherwise provided in this article, or otherwise provided by rule, on and after January 1, 2024 a covered building shall not have annual building emissions higher than the annual building emissions limit for such building as determined in accordance with this section based on the occupancy group of the building.» The law came with a package: «LL97 was first enacted in 2019 as part of a package known as the Climate Mobilization Act.» The cap is a limit per square foot, set by how the space is used; each use group has its own limit, and occupancy groups S and U have one. For 2024 to 2029: «For calendar years 2024 through 2029 the annual building emissions limits for covered buildings shall be calculated pursuant to items 1 through 10 of this section.» «10. For spaces classified as occupancy groups S and U: multiply the building emissions intensity limit of 0.00426 tCO2e/sf by the corresponding gross floor area (sf).» And for 2030 to 2034 the limit for occupancy groups S and U is lower: «10. For spaces classified as occupancy groups S and U: multiply the building emissions intensity limit of 0.00110 tCO2e/sf by the corresponding gross floor area (sf).»\n\nPlainly: a business that owns a building of more than 25,000 gross square feet in the city, or a group of buildings on one tax lot of more than 50,000, has a yearly emissions budget for it, and the limit for occupancy groups S and U falls from 0.00426 to 0.00110 tCO2e/sf in 2030.\n\n*Analytical inference:* the law gives occupancy groups S and U their own intensity limit; the texts do not say which kinds of building fall in those groups or whether a particular freight building does. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the occupancy group of each building and whether the business is its owner.\n\n## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action\n\nCOST ALERT: the emissions cap is in force and its penalty is stated on the emissions above the limit, with the limit for occupancy groups S and U falling in 2030. The penalty formula is the difference between the limit and reported emissions, multiplied by $268. The texts state no pass-through of this cost to a tenant or a freight rate.\n\n- A facilities lead at a business that owns or runs a building over 25,000 gross square feet in New York City checks the building's entry and compliance pathway on the DOB Covered Buildings List, and sets the date for the next report, May 1 of each year, in the compliance calendar with the registered design professional who will certify it.\n- A real estate lead at a business that rents such a building asks the owner, at the next lease review, for the building's compliance pathway and its latest reported emissions against its limit.\n\n*Analytical inference:* the first step rests on the owner duties in section 8; the second step rests on the same duty falling on the owner, not the tenant; the texts name no duty on a tenant. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a lease passes any LL97 cost on to the tenant.\n\n## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain\n\nThe texts name these roles: the owner of a covered building, who files and pays; the registered design professional, who certifies the report; the DOB; the building identification number and tax lot, which fix what is covered; and the tenant, who is not named. The DOB puts it on the owner: «Building owners are responsible for verifying the accuracy of all information used for compliance and reporting.» And listing is not a safe harbour: «The presence or absence of any property on this list, or any information displayed about a building, does not relieve a building owner of legal obligations under Local Law 97 or any other applicable law.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a freight business is in the chain as an owner or as a tenant; as a tenant it is not named by the law's duty text. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is the owner for a building it holds under a long lease, and which compliance pathway the building has.\n\n## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis\n\nThe DOB publishes guidance for owners: «Building owners will need to work with a registered design professional, or in limited cases a retro-commissioning agent, to achieve compliance path with the law.» and lists the compliance pathways: «Individual buildings on a BBL may be subject to LL97 under Article 320 beginning in 2024, in 2026, or in 2035, and others may be required to demonstrate compliance just one time under Article 321.»\n\nThe DOB's Covered Buildings List is guidance, not law: «The DOB Sustainability Laws Covered Buildings List (CBL) reflects the current records of the Department as of March 2026.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the pathway decides which year a building first faces a limit, so a building's pathway is the first fact to confirm. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the pathway for each building and any dispute filed on the list.\n\n## 7. Threshold Questions\n\nThe question that decides coverage is size and lot: «LL97 covers: a building that exceeds 25,000 gross square feet two or more buildings on the same tax lot that together exceed 50,000 gross square feet two or more condominium buildings governed by the same board of managers and that together exceed 50,000 gross square feet.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* a freight building below 25,000 gross square feet that is alone on its tax lot is outside the cap on this wording; two such buildings on one lot together over 50,000 are inside. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the gross floor area of each building and lot as the city records show it.\n\n## 8. Substantive Requirements\n\nLimit. «Except as otherwise provided in this article, or otherwise provided by rule, on and after January 1, 2024 a covered building shall not have annual building emissions higher than the annual building emissions limit for such building as determined in accordance with this section based on the occupancy group of the building.»\n\nLimits by period. «For calendar years 2024 through 2029 the annual building emissions limits for covered buildings shall be calculated pursuant to items 1 through 10 of this section.» «For calendar years 2030 through 2034 the annual building emissions limits for covered buildings shall be calculated pursuant to items 1 through 10 of this section.» «No later than January 1, 2023, the commissioner shall establish by rule annual building emissions limits and building emissions intensity limits applicable for calendar years 2035 through 2039 and building emissions limits and building emissions intensity limits applicable for calendar years 2040 through 2049.» «Such limits shall be set to achieve an average building emissions intensity for all covered buildings of no more than 0.0014 tCO2e/sf/yr by 2050.»\n\nLimits for occupancy groups S and U. «10. For spaces classified as occupancy groups S and U: multiply the building emissions intensity limit of 0.00426 tCO2e/sf by the corresponding gross floor area (sf).» «10. For spaces classified as occupancy groups S and U: multiply the building emissions intensity limit of 0.00110 tCO2e/sf by the corresponding gross floor area (sf).»\n\nReport. «By May 1, 2025, and by May 1 of every year thereafter, the owner of a covered building shall file with the department a report, certified by a registered design professional» «Article 320 requires covered buildings to file a report with the Department by May 1, 2025 detailing their annual GHG emissions and then by May 1 of every year after.»\n\nPenalty for excess emissions. «An owner of a covered building who has submitted a report pursuant to section 28-320.3.7 which indicates that such building has exceeded its annual building emissions limit shall be liable for a civil penalty of not more than an amount equal to the difference between the building emissions limit for such year and the reported building emissions for such year, multiplied by $268.»\n\nPenalty for failing to file. «An owner of a covered building subject to a violation for failure to file a report shall be liable for a penalty of not more than an amount equal to the gross floor area of such covered building, multiplied by $0.50, for each month that the violation is not corrected within the 12 months following the reporting deadline»\n\nPenalty rule. «The Department of Buildings (“DOB” or “Department”) is amending section 103-14 to establish penalties for noncompliance with Article 320 of Chapter 3 of Title 28 of the New York City Administrative Code requiring annual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions limits for buildings and to establish a credit for beneficial electrification.»\n\nPathways. «Individual buildings on a BBL may be subject to LL97 under Article 320 beginning in 2024, in 2026, or in 2035, and others may be required to demonstrate compliance just one time under Article 321.»\n\nThe texts state no pass-through of the penalty or of the cost of meeting a limit to a tenant, a customer or a freight rate. No scope limits are stated in section 8 of this document beyond the covered buildings quoted in section 7.\n\n*Analytical inference:* the limit and the penalty fall on the owner of the covered building; the limits tighten in steps in 2030 and 2035. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the penalty or the cost of compliance may be charged to a tenant under a lease, and which limit applies to a mixed-use building.\n\nObligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 16.\n\n## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations\n\nOwners report yearly: «Article 320 requires covered buildings to file a report with the Department by May 1, 2025 detailing their annual GHG emissions and then by May 1 of every year after.» The report is certified: «By May 1, 2025, and by May 1 of every year thereafter, the owner of a covered building shall file with the department a report, certified by a registered design professional» Missing the date has a price: «An owner of a covered building subject to a violation for failure to file a report shall be liable for a penalty of not more than an amount equal to the gross floor area of such covered building, multiplied by $0.50, for each month that the violation is not corrected within the 12 months following the reporting deadline» The text also gives time: an extension may be requested, which «shall not modify the owner’s obligation to comply with the applicable emission limits for such calendar year».\n\n*Analytical inference:* the reporting date is a fixed yearly date, so a calendar entry for May 1 covers it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether an extension has been granted for a given year.\n\n## 11. Operational System Requirements\n\nCOST ALERT: the owner needs measured energy use by fuel for each building to calculate emissions, and a registered design professional to certify the report. A facilities lead at a business that owns a covered building gathers, before the next reporting year starts, the building's electricity, gas and fuel oil use for each month and gives it to the certifying professional.\n\n*Analytical inference:* the step rests on the report sentence in section 8 and the fuel coefficients in the law, which attach emissions to each energy source; the texts do not list the data the report must hold. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the data the DOB report form asks for.\n\n## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases\n\nThe covered building definition has exceptions: «Exceptions: 1. An industrial facility primarily used for the generation of electric power or steam.» Offsets are capped at a share of the calculated emissions limit, not of the building: «Offsets (Maximum allowable deduction is 10% of a building» and «calculated emissions limit)». The DOB lists distributed energy resources as a separate deduction: «Distributed Energy Resources (onsite solar, offsite solar, onsite storage or offsite storage)». Time to adjust is limited: «320.8 and 320.9 adjustment applications due to excessive emissions and special uses or for not-for-profit healthcare or hospital facilities, have closed as of January 1, 2025.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* the DOB lists distributed energy resources as a deduction and caps offsets separately; the texts do not say how much a given building could deduct. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which deductions apply to a given building and whether the adjustment windows are closed for it.\n\n## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives\n\nThe city's separate benchmarking law also has a date and a price: «Failure to submit the report by May 1 will result in a penalty of $500.00.»\n\n*Analytical inference:* benchmarking is a different duty from LL97 and has its own May 1 date. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the building is covered by benchmarking as well.\n\n## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline\n\n- 2019: LL97 was first enacted as part of the Climate Mobilization Act (past)\n- January 1, 2023: the deadline for the commissioner to set limits for 2035 to 2049 by rule (past)\n- January 1, 2024: building emissions limits apply (in force)\n- January 20, 2024: the Article 320 penalty framework rule took effect (in force)\n- January 1, 2025: adjustment applications for excessive emissions and special uses closed (past)\n- May 1, 2025: first annual report due, and by May 1 every year after (past; the next is May 1 of the following year)\n- 2026: Article 320 started for buildings on pathway 1 (past); the next annual report is due May 1 of the following year\n- 2030: stricter limits begin, with the limit for occupancy groups S and U at 0.00110 tCO2e/sf (ahead)\n- 2035: Article 320 starts for pathway 2 buildings and limits for 2035 to 2039 apply (ahead)\n- 2040: limits for 2040 to 2049 apply (ahead)\n- 2050: the average target of no more than 0.0014 tCO2e/sf/yr and net zero (ahead)\n- 2055: the office reports on whether to repeal or amend the requirements (ahead)\n\n*Analytical inference:* the rows give the dates the quoted texts state. *Legal Confirmation Required:* any change to a date since the texts were captured.\n\n## 15. Sources\n\n- LL97 Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reduction, NYC Department of Buildings: https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/codes/ll97-greenhouse-gas-emissions-reductions.page\n- Local Law 97 of 2019, New York City Council: https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/local_laws/ll97of2019.pdf\n- Annual Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions Limits for Buildings, NYC Rules: https://rules.cityofnewyork.us/rule/annual-greenhouse-gas-ghg-emissions-limits-for-buildings/\n- NYC Benchmarking Law (LL84), NYC Department of Buildings: https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/codes/benchmarking.page",
